source.title: Global Divergence, Local Convergence: Representation Geometry in SSMs and Transformers

record.tranche_reason: Measures cross-architecture representational similarity using ZCA-CKA and mutual k-nearest-neighbor overlap, rather than testing the original sources’ methods. It reports both local alignment and global divergence.
record.gate_note: Rows cover cross-model alignment results from CKA and m-KNN. The paper also reports RankMe, IsoScore, PC1 variance and probe/autoencoder results, but these do not directly measure cross-model distance alignment. Random-initialization comparisons appear in Figure 5 without a textual result about convergence across trained seeds.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-architecture representational alignment directly. It compares transformers (Pythia, Falcon) and SSMs (Mamba, FalconMamba) with ZCA-CKA on two corpora, CKA across whitening strengths, and m-KNN on FineWeb-Edu. It also tracks how alignment with Mamba develops across Pythia's training checkpoints. These results bear on whether convergence depends on inputs and measure (V6), and on whether it is incomplete or plateaus (V7). The method differs from the original sources, so the tranche is T2.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is mostly correct. The authors conclude that transformers and SSMs differ sharply in global geometry: transformers are anisotropic and SSMs isotropic. They find matched effective capacity and matched concept-subspace dimensionality. Structural alignment is uneven: high within specific relations and in local token neighborhoods, low over the general corpus. Local alignment emerges early in training (~4%), ahead of global geometry.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ZCA-CKA and mutual k-nearest-neighbor overlap to compare transformer and SSM residual-stream representations; it does not reproduce the methods of the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured alignment depends on input corpus: relation-specific LAMA TREx representations align more than FineWeb-Edu representations. CKA is evaluated with ZCA whitening, and the paper also checks whitening strengths; it reports that the local/global gap remains when whitening is absent. Local alignment is reported at corresponding depths and at an early training checkpoint.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The comparison covers a limited set of language-model architectures and does not test vision-language models, model capability/performance as a predictor of alignment, or causal explanations for shared structure. Several alignment outcomes are presented only in figures. The paper reports sampling and seed stability checks, but these do not address the untested cross-modal and training-data/objective questions.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant measured cross-model alignment result was left out. Global geometry measures and probing/autoencoder results were omitted because they do not directly measure cross-model distance alignment. Figure 5 includes random-initialization entries, but the text gives no result interpreting them as evidence about convergence across independently trained, trained models.

untested.parts: The study reports no trend of cross-architecture alignment with model size or capability. Pairs at 1.4B, 2.8B and 7B appear in Fig. 4, but no scale comparison is drawn. The training-checkpoint result (alignment saturates by 4% of training) concerns a single model's trajectory, not cross-model scaling.
The study has no vision-language or paired image-caption data.
It does not compare same-architecture models trained from different seeds. The random-initialization entries in Fig. 5 are untrained baselines.
It tests no linear maps, stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment.
It compares no neurons, SAE features or circuits. Wang et al. (2025) is only cited.
It does not test out-of-distribution inputs and does not vary k for m-KNN (k=10 is fixed).
It does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause the alignment; Li et al. (2025) on this point is only cited.

missing.what: Maximum-similarity CKA as a function of whitening strength α (0 to 1) for LAMA TREx and FineWeb-Edu. The authors say the local/global gap persists at all α. This bears on V6's dependence on measure settings.

Per-pair 'Mean Max' ZCA-CKA values printed in Fig. 4, including Pythia-1.4B vs Pythia-2.8B, Mamba-2.8B pairs and the Falcon-7B vs FalconMamba-7B pair. Approximately 0.35–0.57 on FineWeb-Edu and 0.80–0.91 on LAMA TREx; pair assignment is unclear in the extracted text.
missing.versions: V6, V7, (V1 if a scale comparison is read from it)

missing.what: m-KNN for early Pythia checkpoints (512 and 1000 steps), and the random-initialization baselines for Pythia and Mamba. These are needed to show that alignment rises and then plateaus, and to give the m-KNN baseline.
m-KNN sampling stability: mean standard error 0.0047 across five 2,000-sample batches. ZCA-CKA coefficient of variation: mean 0.15% on FineWeb-Edu and 0.56% on LAMA TREx.

record.verdict_notes: The reader labelled V6 'limits_scope', but V6 is a challenge version and these results behave as it says, so the label is changed to supports. The rows carried one state across V6 and V7, which does not fit; links were narrowed accordingly. V1 stays untested, though Fig. 4 contains pairs at several sizes that a researcher could inspect. The checkpoint saturation is also weakly relevant to V1's 'more capable' clause, but capability is not measured. The authors cite Gröger et al. (2026), which reports local-but-not-global convergence, as consistent with their finding.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether alignment between independently trained models rises with model scale or capability/performance.
No paired image-caption or vision-language model comparison.
Does not report whether separately trained models of the same architecture share features or subspaces across initializations.
Does not test mappings, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
Does not compare recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Tests dependence on input corpus and reports a whitening robustness check, but does not test out-of-distribution inputs or systematically vary m-KNN k.
Shows global-versus-local differences and early emergence of local alignment. It does not establish that shared training data or objectives cause the alignment, or that alignment plateaus.

rows.subject: Mamba-1.4B vs Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Measured cross-model linear CKA without whitening; reported the layer mean for each corpus.
rows.note: The authors report this as substantially higher alignment than on FineWeb-Edu.
rows.check: This row is the high-alignment arm of the corpus contrast (0.78 vs 0.52 in r2) and is observed for V6. Its V7 link is dropped: 0.78 is fairly high and does not by itself show far-from-complete alignment. The value is a layer mean of maximum-similarity CKA at α=0 (Fig. 9), not plain layer-wise CKA.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix E, Figure 9 discussion: unwhitened layer means.

rows.subject: Mamba-1.4B vs Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Measured cross-model linear CKA without whitening; reported the layer mean for each corpus.
rows.note: The authors contrast this with the higher LAMA TREx alignment, indicating corpus dependence and weaker alignment on the general corpus.
rows.check: 0.52 on FineWeb-Edu against 0.78 on LAMA TREx shows input dependence (V6) and markedly incomplete alignment on the general corpus (V7). The reader's 'partial' understates it: relative to these versions the effect is observed.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix E, Figure 9 discussion: unwhitened layer means.

rows.subject: Mamba-1.4B vs Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Measured ZCA-whitened CKA between representations from the two models.
rows.note: The text describes relation-specific similarity as substantially higher than the general-corpus baseline; no numerical value is stated in the text for this ZCA result.
rows.check: The value is not purely figure-only: Fig. 4 prints 'Mean Max' values, roughly 0.80–0.91 for LAMA TREx pairs, though the extracted text garbles which pair each belongs to. This row is the high arm of the V6 corpus contrast. The V7 link is dropped because high relation-specific alignment does not show incompleteness.

rows.subject: Fully trained transformer and SSM models (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: Includes models at 1.4B, 2.8B, and 7B; aggregate details not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared mutual nearest-neighbor overlap for identical tokens across model representations.
rows.note: The text reports remarkably high overlap for fully trained transformer and SSM models and says they track changes across depth in parallel. This is an aggregate description, not a per-pair numeric result.
rows.check: For V6, this is the measure-contrast arm: m-KNN on FineWeb-Edu is 'remarkably high' while ZCA-CKA on the same corpus is low (r4). For V7, the high local overlap counts against 'far from complete' and is used in a limits_scope verdict. Fig. 5 includes random-initialization models, which act as an unrecorded baseline; the baseline should not be 'not stated'.

source_check.correct: V6: observed as the local-measure arm of the contrast with global CKA. V7: cannot_determine from this endpoint alone; high local overlap establishes neither far-from-complete alignment nor a training plateau.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B checkpoint at 5,000 steps vs Mamba-1.4B

rows.operation_detail: Measured m-KNN alignment across intermediate Pythia checkpoints and the Mamba model.

rows.check: Local alignment saturates by 5K steps (~4% of training) and matches Pythia's self-similarity to its final state. This is a plateau, the part of V7 the row bears on. The lower earlier checkpoints (512 and 1000 steps) are not recorded.
